# First-time setup

The first time you open Mini-Me, a window called **GET STARTED** appears. It checks your
computer and installs everything Mini-Me needs. **You only have to press one button** — the app
does the rest and stops only when it needs you.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/setup-get-started.png`\
**Show:** The GET STARTED window as it first appears, with the list of steps and the
*Get Started* button.
:::
<!-- ![The Get Started window](images/setup-get-started.png) -->

## Before you start

- Make sure you are **connected to the internet**.
- Have your **API key** ready (see [What is an API key?](glossary.qmd#api-key)).
- Set aside about **15–30 minutes**. Most of that time is the computer downloading things.
- Your computer may need to **restart once**. Save any other work first.

## How it works

1. Click **Get Started**.
2. The app goes through the list of steps from top to bottom.
   - A step that is running shows its progress right underneath it.
   - A finished step shrinks to a single line with a tick (✓).
3. When a step needs you (for example, to sign in or paste a key), the app **pauses** and tells
   you what to do. Do it, then click **Continue**.
4. When every required step is done, the window says **Ready to run** and the button changes
   to **Done**. Click it and you can start working.

::: {.callout-tip}
Steps marked **Optional** can be skipped. Mini-Me still works without them, but some features
won't be available. You can come back to them at any time (see
[Running the setup again](#running-the-setup-again)).
:::

## The steps, one by one

### 1. Linux support for Windows (WSL)

**What it is:** Mini-Me's "engine" runs inside a small Linux system that Windows can host,
called **WSL**. You never have to use it directly.

**What you do:**

- If it is missing, the app offers **Install WSL** or **Install Ubuntu**.
- Windows asks for **administrator permission** — click **Yes**.
- A **separate black window** opens and shows the installation. Mini-Me can't show this
  progress itself, so **watch that window** until it finishes.
- If Ubuntu asks you to **create a username and password**, choose any you like and write
  them down. (They are only for this Linux system, not your Windows account.)
- Windows may ask you to **restart**. After restarting, open Mini-Me again; the setup continues
  where it stopped.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/setup-wsl-window.png`\
**Show:** The separate black installation window that opens while WSL / Ubuntu installs.
:::
<!-- ![The WSL installation window](images/setup-wsl-window.png) -->

### 2. Mini-Me backend

**What it is:** the part of Mini-Me that does the actual research work.

**What you do:** nothing. The app copies it into place and installs what it needs. This
takes **a few minutes**. You will see lines of text scrolling under the step — that is normal.

### 3. Python dependencies

**What it is:** extra tools the backend uses (for statistics, charts, and so on).

**What you do:** nothing. This is usually done as part of the step above.

### 4. Conversation storage

**What it is:** makes sure your conversations are **saved to disk**, so you don't lose them
when you close the app.

**What you do:** nothing, unless it shows a problem. If it does, click
**Save conversations to disk**.

### 5. Model API key

**What it is:** the key that lets Mini-Me use an AI company's model. Without it, Mini-Me can't
answer questions.

**What you do:**

1. Copy your API key (from the email or page where you got it).
2. Click in the box and **paste** it (`Ctrl+V`).
3. Click **Save key**.

Your key is kept safely in **Windows' own password store** (Credential Manager) — never in a
normal file.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/setup-api-key.png`\
**Show:** The *Model API key* step with the paste box and the *Save key* button.
:::
<!-- ![Paste your API key and click Save key](images/setup-api-key.png) -->

::: {.callout-note}
The setup asks for a key for the AI company that is selected by default. If your key is from a
different company, click **Skip this step**, finish the setup, and then add the key in
[Settings → Model](settings.qmd#model).
:::

### 6. Asta (required)

**What it is:** **Asta** is a service from the Allen Institute for AI. Mini-Me uses it to
**search scientific papers**, read PDFs, and generate research ideas — most specialists depend
on it, so this step is **required**. Until you sign in, the setup window opens again each time
you start Mini-Me.

**What you do:**

1. The app may first install the Asta tool by itself (about a minute).
2. Then it asks you to **sign in**. A short **code** appears in large letters, with a button
   **Open the sign-in page**.
3. Click the button. Your web browser opens the Asta sign-in page.
4. Type or check the code, and sign in with your account.
5. Go back to Mini-Me — it notices the sign-in by itself and continues.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/setup-asta-signin.png`\
**Show:** The Asta step with the large sign-in code and the *Open the sign-in page* and
*Copy* buttons.
:::
<!-- ![Signing in to Asta](images/setup-asta-signin.png) -->

::: {.callout-tip}
If the browser doesn't open, click **Copy ⧉** next to the button and paste the link into your
browser yourself.
:::

If the step says your account **"can't generate research theories"**, literature search still
works. Only the idea-generation feature needs extra permission — ask your team lead which Asta
account to use, then click **Sign in again**.

### 7. CIP Dataverse (required)

**What it is:** the **CIP Dataverse** is CIP's catalogue of research datasets. Mini-Me searches
it with a small tool that comes with the app.

**What you do:** nothing. This step only checks that the tool is installed. Searching public
datasets needs **no account and no sign-in**.

::: {.callout-warning}
If this step shows a problem, the tool that comes with the app is missing or damaged: setup
can't finish, and Mini-Me **won't find any datasets**. Install the latest Mini-Me update (or
reinstall Mini-Me), then open it again.
:::

## Buttons at the bottom of the window

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Get Started** | Starts going through all the steps automatically. |
| **Working…** | Shown while the app is busy. Just wait. |
| **Continue** | Use it after you have done something the app asked you to do (for example, sign in). |
| **Retry** | Shown when a step failed. Tries that step again. |
| **Re-check instead** | Checks your computer again without running anything. |
| **Done** | Everything required is ready. Closes the window. |
| **Skip for now** | Closes the setup. You can open it again later (see below). |
| **Stop** | Stops the step that is running right now. |

## Running the setup again {#running-the-setup-again}

You can open the setup window again at any time, for example to sign in to Asta again or to
finish a step you skipped:

- Open **Settings** (`Ctrl+,`) → **Backend** → **Run setup checks**, or
- Press `Ctrl+P`, type **setup**, and choose **Run setup checks**.

Mini-Me also opens it by itself if something essential stops working.

## If a step fails

- Read the message under the step — it usually says what went wrong in plain words.
- Click **Retry** to try that step again.
- If it still fails, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).
